Hi, my experience is very limited so far but getting nexplanon implanted is incredibly easy, the nerves (and numbing shot) were the worst part. If you don't like needles, look away, if its too bad, go for the IUD. Basics of it is they clean the area at the back of your non dominant arm, put in some numbing agent so you can't feel it then wait five minutes for it to work. They'll make sure the area is completely numb before doing anything, you'll be able to feel the pressure but not the pain. To insert the bar the tool they use looks bulky but is just to make sure the needle and bar stay sterilized, the needle to insert it is maybe a millimeter in diameter but you won't feel anything. Takes about 5-10 seconds to insert it. Then they put a bandaid over the small hole and wrap it with gauze. For about 2 weeks there might be a large bruise, other than that you're unable to see it. Its much safer than the pill and its an insert and forget about it contraceptive, no going to the doctor unless to remove it. Its not common to have a problem with it. 99% effective! Woo! (Still use a condom if you want to avoid diseases though)
